findings.source_quote: ὑπὸ δὲ τῆς συνεχείας τοῦ πνεύματος χυθῆναι μὴ δυνάμενον εἰς αἵματος φύσιν μετατρέπειν ἔφασκεν τὸν ἐν αὐτῷ ἀέρα
findings.english_quote: Next, he said, it changes the air within it—which cannot be poured out because of the spirit’s cohesion—into the nature of blood
findings.issue: The main rendering is defensible, but the notes do not disclose a material alternative involving both agency and reference. χυθῆναι μὴ δυνάμενον can be understood as neuter, referring to the previously mentioned water as the subject of μετατρέπειν; αὐτῷ can then refer to that water. On this reading, the water cannot flow out because of the spirit’s cohesion and changes the air within itself into blood. Merely mentioning an impersonal alternative does not preserve this reading.
findings.suggested_revision: Expand the note to preserve the water-subject reading explicitly. Explain that the main text instead continues the spirit as agent, attaches χυθῆναι μὴ δυνάμενον to the air, and takes αὐτῷ as referring to the spirit, favoring continuity with the preceding spirit-agent construction. This is interpretive ambiguity, not demonstrated source corruption; no emendation or additional print verification is required. Submit the amended note and main text for fresh review.

findings.source_quote: θεὸς εἶναι οὐ δύνασαι· φοβήθητι τὸν ὄντως θεόν
findings.english_quote: You cannot be a god. Fear the God who truly is.
findings.issue: ὄντως qualifies θεόν: the contrast is between Simon’s inability to be a god and the one who really is God. The draft’s bare “who truly is” leaves the predicate unstated and readily sounds like an existential formulation. “The real God” represents the supplied wording more clearly and preserves the immediate contrast without that additional ambiguity.
findings.suggested_revision: For fresh review, replace “Fear the God who truly is” with “Fear the real God” or “Fear the one who really is God.”
